claim: Solvers pick moves by one-step-lookahead hill-climbing on visible goal progress (maximisation); first, second and third move correct rates in the six-coin ring task match the CSP prediction (11.3% vs 11%; 30% vs 33%; 6/6 vs 100%), and first-move coins-on-ring exceeds chance (4.42 vs 4.08).
agent_test: Log the greedy-progress choice rate of the agent on a toy with a known trap (coin or Rush Hour variants); compare its move choices with a one-step progress maximiser at equal tokens.

claim: Which goal the solver holds sets difficulty: changing only the start layout (partial ring 4/27 vs straight line 11/27, chi2 4.52, p<.05) or showing the correct goal example (two-group 8/9 and 10/11 vs 3/11 abstract) changes solving; showing the competing ring goal does not help.
agent_test: Give the agent the same puzzle with a goal example for the true vs the tempting goal; test whether restating the goal criterion before acting changes solve rate at equal tokens.

claim: Moves that look like progress but enter a dead end lower solution rates (eight-coin layouts with many strategic moves; six-coin vs ten-coin 10/48 vs 36/48 within 5 min; straight-line vs partial-ring start). Layout alone shifts difficulty.
agent_test: Build a trap-density knob on a puzzle family; check that agent solve rate falls with trap density as in humans, and whether a progress-vs-criterion check restores it.

claim: Hints that only say go outside the box, or give visual cues, do not help the nine-dot problem; base rate is under 5%. Only hints that give away part of the solution help.
agent_test: Calibration: test a generic reset prompt against a content-specific hint when the agent is stuck.

claim: Lookahead depth varies by person (about 32% / 32% / 36% for depth 1 / 2 / 3, MacGregor 2001 via Jones 2003; 37% zero, 31.5% one or two, 21% three for weighing) and spatial, not verbal, working memory predicts drawing outside the grid (6 of 7, chi2 4.15, p=.04; r=.452 vs .199). The Chein test is indirect (span as a stand-in for lookahead).
agent_test: Vary the agent's explicit lookahead budget (steps simulated before commit); see if solve rate on trap puzzles rises with depth at equal tokens.

claim: Progress monitoring vs representational change: in an unlimited-move car-park task, easy practice and a rotated board raised solving (7/13 normal vs 24/26 combined; Fisher p about .01, recomputed .0098), favouring representational change; monitoring predicted no effect. One study, N=39. Criterion failure needs a move budget, so it never fires in an unlimited-move task (Jones 2003), which weakens this as a test of CSP as stated.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: criterion-failure trigger alone vs trigger plus forced re-representation of the state.

claim: Combined account: progress monitoring says when to leave the current search; representational change says how. Relaxing constraints alone did not help the ten-penny task (7% vs 10% control) but adding a maximisation criterion lifted solving to 72% (21/29 vs 3/30).
agent_test: Ablate the agent: re-representation prompt alone, search-criterion prompt alone, both, at equal tokens, on a two-obstacle puzzle set.
audit_note: Only Oellinger et al. 2017 (a28 and b14 are the same paper) supports the numbers and the combined account; Jones 2003 is a test of two theories that finds representational change better and does not propose merging them.

claim: Solvers vary attempts more, repeat less, and use the key feature (intersections) earlier than non-solvers (variation .59 vs .43, d=.67; attempts 8.4 vs 10.9; 47% vs 26% early use).
agent_test: Compute a variation rate (distinct approaches per attempt) on agent traces; test if low variation predicts failure and whether forced variation helps.

claim: Impasse is observable in behaviour: the longest fixation precedes the key move in every solver (30/30), using a per-person threshold (mean + 2 SD). A neural model names inactivity and repeated attempts as impasse correlates.
agent_test: Define an agent impasse as a per-run outlier (latency or token burst, repeated actions); verify it precedes the key move in logged solved traces.

claim: Human warmth ratings on insight problems stay flat and jump only about 15 s before solution (N=25; interaction F=20.60), so felt progress is a poor early predictor; progress must be computed from task state.
agent_test: Compare a self-reported agent progress score with a state-computed one (CSP ratio) as predictors of eventual solving.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-26 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Training on non-dot turns can raise or lower nine-dot success depending on content (Kershaw 63% vs 27% vs 37%; Spiridonov 37.5% vs 78.1%), which a pure lookahead story does not predict. Acting with hands did not help in a failed replication (N=105/88/74) and an implicit motor-learning benefit was not confirmed.
agent_test: Test whether a worked example of the key move type in the prompt helps more than generic examples.

claim: An executable CSP model exists (ACT-R, nine-dot). PRODIGI (Ormerod, MacGregor, Banks, Rusconi 2024, unpublished ms under review) extends CSP rather than replacing it: it keeps the progress-ratio monitor and adds idea discovery after impasse. Only a secondary chapter by the same group was read; the PRODIGI paper itself was not found.
agent_test: Implement the CSP ratio as code on agent puzzle states; compare predicted vs actual move choice.

claim: LLM self-reported progress is unreliable mid-task and good at start and end: 7 of 11 models comply with a reporting duty (93.2-100% of checkpoints), 4 comply at only 0.6-10.1%; compliant models are right at 90.6-99.4% pre-action; mid-task reports are often wrong. Verified against the source text.
agent_test: Compare self-reported stage with a harness-computed progress measure at checkpoints; use the harness measure as the stuck signal.

claim: Uncertainty signals (verbal confidence, entropy, consistency) predict failure well only at the end of a trajectory (AUROC .85) and poorly mid-way (<=.60 at 50%). Token entropy did not reliably predict when a spontaneous shift helps (pooled OR 0.77, CI .58-1.02, N=723,200).
agent_test: Do not rely on entropy or verbal confidence as a mid-run trigger; test an external state-based trigger against an entropy trigger at equal tokens.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace strategy shifts in small GRPO reasoning models are rare (6.31% of traces) and go with lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%; this is pooled over all models and domains, N=723,200; the Qwen2.5-1.5B row is 7.65% shifted, accuracy 3.95% vs 20.42%). In eight open reasoning models (up to DeepSeek-R1-0528) on math, over 90% of post-answer reflections are confirmatory and under 2% are corrective, using 16.8-47.8% of tokens for a 1.4-3.5 point gain. Forced external reconsideration is the better lever than waiting for an aha. Observational; shift and difficulty are confounded; no closed frontier model tested.
agent_test: Compare spontaneous revision with harness-forced revision at a computed impasse, at equal tokens.

claim: Excess switching and looping mark failure: wrong answers use 225% more tokens and 418% more thought switches; low-temperature loops reach 76% in a 1.5B model vs 37% in 32B; penalising switch words raised AIME pass@1 (QwQ 38.3 to 44.1).
agent_test: Detect loops by text similarity and action repeats; test halt-and-reframe at loop detection vs continuing, at equal tokens.

claim: Deployed stuck rules are simple counters (same action 3-4+ times, 5 low-progress scores in a row, nonzero return codes, one file edited too often) and help: +5.0 pp on SWE-bench Verified (33.5% vs 28.5%); ALFWorld +40 pp with a progress gate. Gains come bundled with other components. Vendor docs (OpenRouter observe 2/block 3/stop 6; DeepEval 3 and 6; OneUptime 3 and 20) publish thresholds with no ablation or false-positive data.
agent_test: Port a counter-based stuck detector to the agent; ablate thresholds and measure resolved rate at equal tokens.

claim: Predicting step progress as a residual delta, and scoring every step instead of the final answer, improves search and error catching (tree plus step value 0.309 vs random-choice tree 0.215; step scoring AUC about .9 vs verbalised .556).
agent_test: Replace absolute self-scores with per-step delta estimates from a separate call; compare with random pruning at equal tokens.

claim: No study was found that tests LLMs on nine-dot, coin or matchstick problems with a progress-criterion measure; CSP is untested on language models. LLM insight benchmarks (BRAINTEASER 53-63% vs humans 92%; NazoNazo reasoning models 17.6% vs humans 52.9%) are not progress-instrumented. Gap search repeated this: no LLM study of goal inference from abstract goals or of lookahead budgets against greedy traps was found. Rush Hour LLM papers exist (CAST, MentisOculi) but do not measure greedy traps.
agent_test: Run the agent on text versions of the six-coin and ten-coin problems and log whether it takes the coins-on-ring greedy move.

claim: Verifier failure: models sometimes write the correct answer in their reasoning yet do not accept it (5.23-39.34% of wrong answers across four models).
agent_test: Check agent traces for correct intermediate answers rejected later; test an answer-recognition step.

claim: In a symbolic two-move matchstick task (N=120), most proposed moves reduce distance to goal (85.46% of 509 equations), yet whether the solution move is greedy has no effect on solving (F(1,116)=1.66 ns) while giving a constraint-relaxing move helps far more than a value move (F(1,116)=45.15). Move choice is greedy; difficulty follows representational depth. This goes against CSP as the main source of difficulty for this task.
agent_test: On a symbolic text puzzle, compare a trigger that forces re-representation at criterion failure against a trigger that only adds lookahead, at equal tokens.

claim: The CSP ratio needs a resource denominator. Under the definition in Jones 2003 criterion failure never fires in an unlimited-move task. An agent harness must therefore set an explicit budget (steps or tokens left) and compute distance left divided by budget left.
agent_test: Run the same puzzle with and without a stated step budget and log when the ratio first exceeds 1.

claim: Early correctness signal exists inside open-weight models but not in text-level uncertainty: hidden-state probes reach AUC 0.84 at 4 reasoning tokens against 0.59 for entropy plus length (Qwen3-8B, MATH, 1,500 prefixes), but most of this tracks item difficulty, and hidden-state horizons are myopic (final answer planned about one step ahead on compositional tasks). Not usable with an API-only agent.
agent_test: If open weights are used, probe at pivot tokens; otherwise compute progress from task state only.

claim: Existing monitor designs for LLM agents have no head-to-head tests of triggers. The Cognitive Companion (LLM check every 2 steps, or probe at 0.55) was run on 6 essay-like tasks, 3 runs each, with no threshold ablation and no false-positive rate; stuck-loop vendors give thresholds with no data. Gaps 2 and 7 are open.
agent_test: Three-arm trigger comparison (counter, entropy, computed criterion failure) at equal tokens with false-positive logging.

claim: No independent replication of the Chronicle 2004 move statistics (cell N=19) was found in the 30 citing records indexed in Europe PMC; citation APIs for wider coverage were rate-limited. Treat as unreplicated.
agent_test: Do not calibrate the agent greedy-move rate to the human 11%/30%/100% figures.
